amd.reviewed_definition: Linux6.8 lists AMD IOMMU options including off, force_enable, force_isolation and page-table options; on is not a supported option. intel_iommu=on explicitly enables the Intel driver. Do not substitute force_enable: it overrides known-buggy-platform handling.

amdparser.reviewed_definition: The AMD parameter parser has no on branch; unknown strings are skipped without setting an enable flag. Detection initializes discovered supported AMD IOMMU hardware subject to firmware/global disable and other prerequisites. This does not prove any particular motherboard is configured.

ubuntu_iommu.reviewed_definition: Enable firmware virtualization/IOMMU, inspect dmesg and IOMMU groups, and isolate the device for passthrough. Recent Ubuntu kernels normally initialize supported IOMMUs automatically; hardware-specific tuning may still be necessary. Nouveau can need blacklisting to release a device.

fstab.reviewed_definition: fstab supports filesystem UUID= identifiers and recommends persistent identifiers because device-name order can change. PARTUUID identifies partitions separately. The adjacent UUID= mount example needs the filesystem UUID.

raid.reviewed_definition: RAID0 stripes data across component devices and has no redundant copy/parity; losing a component can lose the array. Redundant arrays can continue in a degraded state, but further faults can exceed their redundancy. Monitoring component/array health is useful; redundancy itself does not require a person first noticing a fault.

nc.reviewed_definition: nc defaults to TCP; -v prints verbose information, -z checks listening ports without application data, -u selects UDP, and -w2 bounds connection/idle waiting to two seconds. These options are the OpenBSD-family nc syntax used on macOS and Ubuntu netcat-openbsd; availability/version is a local prerequisite. UDP send success is not receipt proof.
